It's been just over a year since I took control of this subverse and so I had decided to update the sticky.

At the time I took control, I was considering the possibility of a large exodus from Reddit and quickly grabbed this subverse in an attempt to prevent it being snatched by the moderators who had ruined large swaths of Reddit.

This exodus didn't really happen and so this subverse has been relatively quiet. I do appreciate the drips of content people have been posting and have remained committed to moderating this place (admittedly, I have never had to delete anything more than a single piece of spam).

My idea for this subverse is for it to be a lightly moderated forum for the discussion of the United Kingdom, with an emphasis on freedom of expression; clearly there is a demand for this, as lots of subreddits have appeared with a similar focus. However, the usual trajectory of all these communities bothers me. I have noticed a polarisation of the internet of sorts whereas only two different kinds of political communities exist: you have heavily moderated left-wing communities and free-speech right-wing communities. As a Christian and a Libertarian, I don't quite fit into either but I digress.

This subverse has very few rules. It really is just follow the site-wide rules and stick to the topic (the United Kingdom). I decided to drop the rule of no direct abuse, as I don't really see a point in it: ditto for not editorialising titles (although I will make flairs to identify when this happens). If you are offended by anything written on this subverse, then tough. Hopefully, continuing to post good content and having good discussions will grow the community further.

So that's my waffle (currently on two-weeks holiday with little to do, if that makes it any less sad).
